### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7613660d16840598b473c66f9605f83f6ea4552` — the merge of head `d0bbf71f7055f889e6343eec78984df456227c6f` into base `e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f7613660d16840598b473c66f9605f83f6ea4552 && git checkout f7613660d16840598b473c66f9605f83f6ea4552
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee d0bbf71f7055f889e6343eec78984df456227c6f && git checkout -B drift-repro e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee && git merge --no-ff d0bbf71f7055f889e6343eec78984df456227c6f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `136a7b679f4e48ba30b779607bda0b89bf492970`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup.app.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`filterAppForUserWithReason`, `holdsRequiredPermissions`), packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts, packages/cli/test/setup-diagnostics-audience.pin.test.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **Mechanics are right.** A group's `requiredPermissions` prunes its subtree before children are judged, so the old `manage_platform_settings` gate on `group_diagnostics` could never let a `view_all_audit_log`-only auditor see the Audit Log entry. Moving the gate onto each entry fixes that: Sessions and Notification Events keep `manage_platform_settings`, and Audit Log takes `LEDGER_AUDIT_CAPABILITY` (`view_all_audit_log`). The per-caller wire pin shows an empty Diagnostics group is not served, so members holding neither capability still see no group, and the platform administrator still sees all three entries.
- **must-fix M1: the narrowing arm is declared as widening.** `holdsRequiredPermissions` is all-of (`required.every(...)`), so the entry cannot be gated on "either capability", and the move is not pure widening. A custom set granting `manage_platform_settings` without `view_all_audit_log` was served `nav_audit_logs` by `GET /meta/app/setup` and is not served it at this head. The changeset says so itself ("One custom-set audience moves the other way"). That audience can still use the page: `audit-log-read-visibility.ts` serves a non-holder the organization-attributed ledger rows. So a working entry is withdrawn from a served answer. That is the same class as #33314's arms (a changed outcome on a published read for an existing caller). Declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (the single arm; AGENTS.md), add a **BREAKING** paragraph whose fix is "grant `view_all_audit_log` to that set, or open the page by URL", and the one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)` fits: nothing stored or authorable moves). Text-only; the code can stay.
- nit N1 (already in the changeset, keep it): the slot no longer gates contributions, so a third-party entry contributed into `group_diagnostics` without its own `requiredPermissions` becomes visible to every member. No in-tree contributor is affected (only platform-objects and plugin-audit contribute there). The "If you contribute into `group_diagnostics`" paragraph is the right place for it. It could also go in the BREAKING paragraph, since it is an exposure change for those contributors.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit` is right for a non-protocol change, widening or narrowing (AGENTS.md). Only the arm and the banner are wrong.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The console sidebar guard applies the same group-prunes-first rule (per the code comment), and it reads the served app, so no UI change is owed.
- CI at this head when read (17:20Z): 14 success, 16 skipped, 18 in progress, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Gating an entry on the capability that governs its data, rather than on its container's admin power, is the right model for separation of duties. It matches `group_configuration`. Without an any-of gate, a custom-set narrowing is unavoidable, and the platform's own sets are unaffected. Accepting it is a reasonable trade, provided it is declared. The design holds; only the declaration needs to change.

### ① Derived judgments

The **BREAKING** paragraph gives the fix ("grant `view_all_audit_log` to that set, or open the page by URL") and the unchanged page behaviour, and covers third-party contributors into `group_diagnostics` (my N1). There is exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, which fits because nothing stored or authorable moves. The title and summary carry `!`, and the PR body's risk line matches. The author reports `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it as BREAKING + bang + narrowing.
- Everything else in my first record holds unchanged at this head: the per-entry gates, the all-of `holdsRequiredPermissions`, the empty group not served, and the shipped sets unaffected.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on both packages with the BREAKING banner, right for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md).

### ③ Boundary flags

- The author says the full dogfood battery owed by the narrowing arm is running on this head and will be reported on the PR. The ACCEPT must cite it, and must re-read every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged: gating the entry on the capability that governs its data is the right separation-of-duties model, and the one custom-set narrowing is now declared with its remedy.
